extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent applicants, trademark examiners, and IP stakeholders (practitioners and public)
extracted.subtask_description: USPTO performance objectives, programs, and metrics for enhancing and measuring patent and trademark quality, timeliness, IT delivery, and stakeholder outreach. Covers examiner training, review forms, pilots, PTAB systems, and trademark quality/performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality — correctness and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent quality is central ... it is critically important that the USPTO issue patents that are both correct and clear. Historically the USPTO’s primary focus has been on correctness, but the evolving patent landscape has challenged the agency to increase its focus on clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency assesses both correctness (legal/technical correctness of decisions) and clarity (clear reasoning, claim interpretation, and record) as dual pillars of patent quality; programs and trainings are oriented to improving both dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Review Form — capture of correctness and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Master Review Form captures both correctness and clarity information via a series of standardized questions. The form was built by using smart form logic so reviewers only see applicable sections/questions for a particular review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by reviewers in Office of Patent Quality Assurance and Technology Centers to consistently document and access office action quality review data; developed using public feedback (Federal Register comments, workshops).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Metrics Program — develop new patent quality metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Quality Metrics Program is developing new, world-class patent quality metrics by using existing data, such as Quality Index Report (QIR) data, and new data, such as Master Review Form data. These metrics will replace the Quality Composite Score used since FY 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric development uses stakeholder feedback (Federal Register comments) and aims to provide improved, defensible measures of patent quality for internal assessment and public reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the Record — best practices for prosecution record clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clarity of the Record Pilot is identifying best practices for enhancing the clarity of particular aspects of the prosecution record, namely claim interpretation, reasons for allowance, and interview summaries, and is exploring the impact of implementing these best practices during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot identifies concrete practices (e.g., clearer reasons for allowance, better interview summaries) and evaluates effects on examination outcomes and record usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: P3 (Panel Post-Prosecution) — after-final amendment process
rubrics_metrics.description: P3 permits an applicant to submit an after-final amendment for consideration by a panel of examiners, present oral arguments to the panel, and then receive a detailed explanation of the panel’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines popular aspects from AFCP 2.0 and the Pre-Appeal Pilot to provide a structured after-final review path and clearer explanations to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Grant Outcomes Program — integrate post-grant outcomes into examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Program objectives: (1) enhance patentability determinations in applications related to patents undergoing an AIA trial; (2) provide targeted examiner training on best practices gathered from post-grant proceedings; (3) provide examiners with periodic reviews of post grant outcomes focusing on technology sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes a Post Grant Outcomes Pilot that notifies examiners when they have an application related to a patent involved in an AIA trial, streamlines access to AIA trial contents, and gathers best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview Specialist Program — interview practice and policy expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interview Specialist Program has identified and trained interview specialists in all Technology Centers to be subject matter experts on interview practice and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview specialists assist applicants and examiners with interviews, including facilitating technical issues; objective is to improve interview quality and utility to prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Patent Publication Quality — image quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Design Patent Publication Quality Program has developed new procedures for improving the image quality of published design patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on publication image standards to improve the clarity and usability of published design patent documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the Record Training — improve clarity and reasoning in office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Training program that has trained examiners on numerous topics, including 35 U.S.C. § 101, 112(a), 112(b), 112(f), and reasons for allowance, with tips and techniques on how examiners can improve the clarity of their office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training delivered via instructor-led modules, workshops, and computer-based training; aimed at improving writing, reasoning, and statutory application in office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Pre-Examination Search Pilot — pre-exam search availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot exploring ways to make a pre-examination search available automatically in patent applications to provide examiners with a strong foundation for their own search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective is to improve examiner search efficiency and the quality of prior art identification by surfacing useful pre-exam search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC Awareness Campaign — ensure examiner use of search tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) Awareness Campaign has publicized to examiners the tools and resources for searching prior art that are currently available in STIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes use of existing search resources to support higher-quality prior art searching and office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluate QPIDS Program — improve QPIDS
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reevaluate QPIDS Program is currently evaluating ways to improve the QPIDS program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic review intended to refine processes that route applications for additional review, to better support quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder training and outreach (Patent Quality Community Symposium / Patent Quality Chats / STEPP)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO holds Patent Quality Community Symposium, Patent Quality Chats webinars, and the Stakeholder Training on Examination Practice and Procedure (STEPP) to provide information, gather public input, and educate external stakeholders on examination practice and why examiners make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symposia and webinars include presentations and Q&A; STEPP offers in-person courses based on examiner training materials to improve external stakeholder understanding and promote higher-quality applicant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PE2E (Patent end-to-end) processing — modernize examiner workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Once fully deployed, the USPTO’s PE2E system will provide examiners with an improved way of processing patent applications, integrating activities currently managed across separate systems into a central place, and leveraging modern technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes replacement of legacy tools, integrated office action and search tools, and workflow improvements designed to increase accuracy and efficiency of application processing and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM stabilization and Reporting System improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stabilize the Patent Application Location and Monitoring (PALM) legacy system and improve the Reporting System for examiners and managers to increase usage and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System stabilization supports reliable access to application data and examiner productivity; part of broader IT modernization.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAV (Docket and Application Viewer) deployment and training
rubrics_metrics.description: DAV is a customizable, searchable tool to help examiners manage their workload and prioritize tasks; the entire patent-examining corps has received training on DAV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widespread adoption (over 65% usage three or more days a week at time of report) expected to help increase patent quality via better workload management and searchability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action and search tool capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned office action capabilities will allow the patent-examination corps to write their office action and to fill out the appropriate forms and workflow for having that office action type approved for communication with the applicant. Search will be a high-performance tool that will find prior art supporting complex Boolean searches, reviewing results, hit terms, and documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced IT tools are designed to support clearer, better-documented office actions and more effective prior art searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: One Portal Dossier (OPD) public access — integrated global dossier access
rubrics_metrics.description: Deployed public access to One Portal Dossier (OPD), an IP5 initiative to provide 'secure, one-stop access and management to global patent applications.' The USPTO will serve as the providing office and integrate OPD with WIPO Centralized Access to Search and Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPD expands searchable coverage of patent documents worldwide, supporting thorough prior art searches and work sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Center / eMod — eCommerce modernization and text application filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizing eCommerce capabilities and integrating MyUSPTO; Patent Center will be a unified interface for patent applications with a pilot to receive text patent applications; eMod will simplify authentication and improve functionality for applicants and examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal is a simpler, more user-friendly electronic patent application process that improves efficiency, communication, and patent quality; replacement of EFS-Web and PAIR with integrated Patent Center over 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional outreach and education — stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand regional presence, offer education and outreach programs (meetings, roundtables, seminars) targeted at aspiring entrepreneurs, innovators, students, and practitioners to explain IP concepts and USPTO services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs include Patents 4 Patients, IP Horizon Scanning Tool, roundtables with PTRCs, seminars on reviews & petitions; objective is to help applicants file and prosecute higher-quality applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Ombudsman Program — assist applicants with prosecution breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patents Ombudsman Program helps applicants or their representatives with issues that arise during patent application prosecution and can assist in getting applications back on track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program provides presentations emphasizing proactive resolution of common inquiries and is available online; intended to help small businesses and pro se inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB resource allocation — maintain timely, high-quality decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB will closely monitor filing trends and make adjustments to staffing requirements to balance workload with human capital resources and maintain timeliness and quality in AIA trials and appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because AIA petition volumes are hard to predict, PTAB considers manager-to-employee ratios, hearing/admin support, and recruitment (e.g., hiring administrative patent judges) to manage workload and meet statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB E2E system — integrated filing and fee processing for AIA trials
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB End-to-End (E2E) is a fully integrated IT system using a web browser step‑by‑step filing program to enable petitioners and patent owners to provide metadata, upload PDF documents, and interface with Fee-Processing Next Generation (FPNG) for paying fees. Initially supports inter partes review, post-grant review, and covered business method review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB E2E replaces PRPS for trial types and will evolve to replace PRPS for derivation proceedings and integrate appeal decision functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average First Action Pendency (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: Trademark Average First Action Pendency (Months). Target: 2.5 to 3.5 months. First action pendency is the length of time between receipt of a trademark application and when the USPTO makes a preliminary decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a timeliness target and managed by aligning examination capacity with workload (hiring, overtime, incentives, details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average Total Pendency (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: Trademark Average Total Pendency (Months). Target: 12.0 months. Average total pendency is the average number of months from date of filing to notice of abandonment, notice of allowance, or registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitored for stakeholder decision-making and process improvements to sustain optimal pendency results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark First Action Compliance Rate (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: This measure is the percentage of applications reviewed meeting the criteria for decision making for the first Office action under the Trademark Act. Target reported (e.g., 95.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates examination quality at first Office action; tracked via in-process review evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Final Compliance Rate (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: This measure is the percentage of applications reviewed meeting the criteria for decision making for registration based on the examiner’s approval or denial of the application including first Office actions. Target reported (e.g., 97.0%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates overall examination quality on final decisions; tracked via in-process review evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Exceptional Office Action (quality measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exceptional Office Action quality measure assesses comprehensive excellence in constructing search strategy, preparing supporting evidence, writing the office action, and communicating the decision. The measure has targets (e.g., increasing over time, shown in Table 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holistic approach emphasizing research, writing, legal decision making, and evidence; used for incentive awards and to set quality expectations for examining attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Applications Processed Electronically (E2E processing metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: Trademark Applications Processed Electronically. Targets set over time (e.g., 82% target), with percent of applications processed exclusively electronically from filing to disposition reported (84.8% in FY 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing is beneficial to users and USPTO workflow; fee incentives and outreach aim to increase e-processing and reduce paper handling subsidy effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark quality measurement — adherence to registrability standards and Office action excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality measurement takes into consideration adherence to registrability standards and the comprehensive excellence of Office actions, including research, writing, legal decision making, and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintained through training, feedback, stakeholder engagement, online tools, and process improvements; quality targets (first/final compliance, exceptional office actions) are routinely measured and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examiner training and mentorship standards
rubrics_metrics.description: New examining attorneys are provided with classroom training and work with a mentor for an extended period. Experienced attorneys receive continuing training resources including in-house legal training, case law updates, and industry-specific training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training supports consistent application of law and writing quality; also includes use of IT research resources and external continuing legal education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Next Generation (TMNG) IT modernization — user-centered E2E system
rubrics_metrics.description: TMNG will separate trademark IT infrastructure and implement an integrated IT system for end-to-end electronic processing of trademark applications and registration maintenance, using user-centered design with end users to identify desired features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TMNG redesigns internal systems (FAST 1 replacement) and enhances tools like Trademark Status and Document Retrieval, X-search, and expanded search functionality to support faster, more reliable E2E processing.
